hints.content:
$f$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $f(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals f of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, negative forty-five and the x-intercept negative four and one-half, zero. It continues to increase until the local maximum at negative three and one-half, twenty-eight. Then it decreases through the x-intercept negative two and one-quarter, zero until a local minimum at negative one, negative twenty. Then it increases through the origin and the point one, forty. It continues to increase until the local maximum at two and one-half, ninety. Then it decreases through the point three, seventy and the x-intercept three and three-quarters, zero. The function is highlighted from x equals negative three and one-half to x equals negative one and after x equals two and one-half.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $f$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-4.5<x<-4$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is increasing on this interval
$-0.5<x<0$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is increasing on this interval
$1<x<2$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is increasing on this interval

Therefore, $f$ is decreasing on none of the above intervals.
